body: Nodes that extend Control perform pixel snap by default, unlike Node2Ds. You can control this behavior by disabling **Snap Controls to Pixels** in the Project Settings. See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4947.

Thanks for the reply! Hmm...I tried turning off Snap controls to pixels but I still see it. I also can still see the rapid side-side oscillation using Sprite2D nodes to hold the textures. I actually think it's happening even in the unscaled texture because when I reach the end, I can still see it.

I've tried a few things to see if any of them mitigate it. I tried a few different versions of Godot from 4.3, to 4.1 and even recreated it in 3.6 and I still see this happening (with both sprites and colorrects even with snapping turned off for controls (and of course snap 2d xforms/vertices to pixel off as well). I then tried it on my laptop thinking maybe it was an NVidia issue. However, on the laptop both on Windows and on Linux (fedora 42) and using either the intel iGPU (it's a 12th gen intel chip) or the discrete GPU (NVidia RTX A1000 2GB, which I think is roughly equivalent to a 3050) I still see it happening.

It still happens if I use a remote transform to drag the camera along. The only thing I was able to notice was if I parented the camera to the root and lerp'd the camera to the "ship" either with a standard lerp or for example
```
extends Sprite2D
@onready var camera_2d: Camera2D = $"../Camera2D"

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	position += Vector2(10.0 * delta, 0.0)
	camera_2d.position = Vector2(move_toward(camera_2d.position.x, position.x, 0.1),camera_2d.position.y)
```
Then the ship moves along but the background sprite2Ds will move along in discrete chunks and I no longer see them vibrating back and forth. If I use the frame delta for the move_toward delta I still see it moving in little chunks but less so than with a larger value of move_towards delta, but obviously the "ship" starts drifting past the camera. The "vibration" does stop though. Not sure if any of that helps?

Edit: It almost seems like as the camera scrolls to the next pixel over, and the background is scrolled one pixel to the left, and (maybe just the edges?) are caught between its current and future position and is displaying one then the other at 60hz, then is oscillating between the next. I have uploaded a 1/8x speed video of my monitor to show what's happening using the above project. The background mountain is a Sprite2d and the white and red box in the first half are sprite2ds with unscaled solid color PNGs (the second half showing the edge has a white and pink colorrect). What's interesting about that is that the mountain in the first half is moving very smoothly since they're all siblings they should in theory all be moving similarly, but (at least the edges of) the colored Sprite2Ds or ColorRects are moving in relation to the mountain sprite.  You can see though when we get to the edge of the sprite2d border for the large mountain sprite, there seems to be some pulsing at the border, though the rest of the sprite seems to be panning smoothly.
